newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: MOST S.KOREAN CHAEBOL TOLD TO CUT DEBT GUARANTEES.
newsitem.headline: MOST S.KOREAN CHAEBOL TOLD TO CUT DEBT GUARANTEES.

text.p: South Korea's Fair Trade Commission said on Monday 80 affiliates at 24 of the nation's top 30 conglomerates had to cut debt payment guarantees for their sister firms to below their shareholders' equity by the end of next March.
A commission report said such debt payment guarantees by the 80 companies outpaced their shareholders' equity by a combined 6.7 trillion won as of April 1.
The Sunkyong and Keopyung groups topped the list with seven affiliates each having debt payment guarantees in excess of their shareholders' equity, the report said.
Six affiliates each of the Hyundai and Miwon groups had debt payment guarantees amounting to more than their shareholders' equity, the report said.
Meanwhile, debt payment guarantees by all affiliates of the 30 chaebol totalled 33.1 trillion won as of April 1, down from 35.2 trillion won a year earlier, it said.
